inputs_used: content/posts/wedding-ceremony-script-australia/01-brief.json (slug and round only, as instructed by the orchestrator)

first_impression.reaction: My assistant found this while checking how we would make the marriage legal in Sydney if the celebration is somewhere else. She kept reading because it is calm, quotes the law and gets to the point. I would not read it myself. I would get a three-line summary: what the celebrant has to say, the witnesses, and the fact that an Australian celebrant cannot marry us abroad. That is useful. It tells me nothing about whether this company can handle a wedding like ours, but to be fair, that is not what the page is for.

journey.reaction: Good. Short, confident, not eager. This is the tone I expect.

journey.section: What the law requires in an Australian wedding ceremony
journey.quote: The celebrant must also meet each of you separately and in person beforehand, and must be physically present to solemnise the marriage, together with the two of you and 2 witnesses.
journey.reaction: This matters for us. Neither of us lives in Australia, so my assistant needs to plan the meetings around our trips. Clear and sourced.

journey.section: The Australian wedding ceremony script, word for word
journey.quote: For a small legal ceremony before a larger celebration, this is the core with nothing added.
journey.reaction: This is the part that applies to us: a small private legal ceremony with family, then the real wedding. Good that it is laid out with nothing extra.

journey.section: The Australian wedding ceremony script, word for word
journey.quote: If this ceremony is one moment in a longer weekend, with guests flying in and a venue to secure, [Wedded Concierge] plans the whole celebration around it.
journey.reaction: Understated, and it reads as planning rather than selling. Fine. It still does not tell me if they have managed several hundred guests or a closed property, but I would not expect that here.

journey.section: Witnesses, the signing and the paperwork on the day
journey.quote: Within 14 days of the marriage, your celebrant must submit the marriage paperwork to the registry of births, deaths and marriages in the state or territory where you married.
journey.reaction: Clear. But it makes me ask straight away who can see that record once it is registered. Discretion is my first concern and the page is silent on it.

journey.section: Marrying overseas or holding a symbolic ceremony
journey.quote: If you are overseas now, you can complete the notice of intended marriage from abroad when you plan to marry in Australia.
journey.reaction: Directly useful for someone in Dubai. My assistant would flag this one.

journey.section: Marrying overseas or holding a symbolic ceremony
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world as your single point of contact from start to finish, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One point of contact, anywhere, is the right promise. Nothing here suggests they handle our size or work with a private security team, but it is not off-putting either.

journey.section: Plan the day around the words
journey.quote: When the ceremony is set, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: 'Quotes in AUD' and 'inclusions' make it sound like I am choosing from a set package. That is the one line that makes it feel standard rather than private. The time zone part is fine.

unanswered_questions: Once the marriage is registered with the state registry, who can see or request that record? Is there any way to keep it private?

If our family also has a religious ceremony with an officiant from our own community, can that be the legal ceremony in Australia, or do we still need an authorised celebrant? (The page points to a separate guide but does not say.)
Can the legal ceremony be held privately at a closed property with only family and the two witnesses present?
Has Wedded Wonderland planned celebrations of several hundred guests, and can they work with a family's own security team? Nothing on this page says.

turn_offs_found.quote: When the ceremony is set, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Inclusions' and 'quotes in AUD' is package and price language. I do not want to be told about quotes on an advice page; I want to know what is possible.

would_share_with: My assistant, who would keep the short legal script and the overseas section for the family office file

cta_reaction.quote: When the ceremony is set, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit. Start the conversation with [Wedded Concierge].
cta_reaction.why: I do not enquire from a blog link. Someone I trust would have to introduce them. If my assistant had already been told about them, this page would not count against them. It is accurate and calm. But nothing here would make me reach out myself.

top_3_changes: Closing line: remove the package and price wording. Old: "When the ceremony is set, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit." New: "When the ceremony is set, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and confirms every detail in writing before you commit."

If a source exists, add one line in 'Witnesses, the signing and the paperwork on the day' on who can access a registered marriage record. This is a source-pack question, not a copy edit, so leave it out if it cannot be sourced.
